definition: A hindrance of aversion, hostility, or ill will toward what is resisted.
notes: The project uses ill will as the default for this hindrance because that is how Dhammarato names it throughout the 2014–2026 talk transcripts (about 1,000 uses of ill will, against no uses of aversive distraction); ill will also matches abyāpāda (non-ill-will) and the ill-will compounds. It names aversion functioning as a hindrance to practice and to unification of mind. Aversive distraction, the earlier house default built on the OSF glossary's distraction family, remains the alternate where continuity with earlier OSF material matters. The family label is now hindrance (nīvaraṇa), and the five members are named the way Dhammarato names them.
